exercises.name: Heel Slide
exercises.summary: Gets the knee bending again without load.
cues: Lie on your back, legs straight
Slide the heel toward your buttock as far as is comfortable
Pause 2 s, then slide back until the knee is fully straight
mistakes: Forcing into a pinch. A stretch is fine; sharp pain is not

exercises.name: Quad Set
exercises.summary: Switches the thigh muscle back on after swelling.
cues: Sit or lie with the leg straight, small rolled towel under the knee
Tighten the thigh to press the back of the knee into the towel
The kneecap should glide upward. Hold, then fully relax
mistakes: Squeezing the buttock instead of the thigh

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.summary: Builds quad strength with the knee locked straight.
cues: Lie on your back, other knee bent with the foot flat
Do a quad set first to lock the knee straight
Lift to the height of the other knee, lower over 3 s
mistakes: The knee bending as the leg lifts. Do quad sets until it stays straight

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.summary: Strengthens the calves, which help support the knee.
cues: Stand tall, fingertips on a wall
Rise onto the balls of both feet, knees straight
Lower slowly over 2–3 s
mistakes: Rolling out onto the little toes

exercises.name: Shallow Wall Sit
exercises.summary: A static thigh hold. Holds like this often ease knee pain.
cues: Back flat on the wall, feet a step out and hip-width apart
Slide down only to a slight bend (30–45°)
Knees over the middle toes, weight in the heels, keep breathing
mistakes: Sliding too deep. Keep it shallow in Phase 1

exercises.name: Terminal Knee Extension
exercises.summary: Trains the last few degrees of straightening.
cues: Loop the band behind the knee, anchored in front at knee height
Start with the knee slightly bent; step back until the band is tight
Straighten the knee fully against the band, squeeze 2 s, release slowly
mistakes: Leaning the hips back instead of straightening the knee

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.summary: Strengthens the glutes, which control where the knee points.
cues: On your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart
Push through the heels until shoulders, hips and knees are in a line
Pause 2 s at the top, lower slowly
mistakes: Arching the low back instead of using the glutes

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.summary: Works the hip muscles that stop the knee caving inward.
cues: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent about 45°, band above the knees
Keep the feet together and the hips stacked
Open the top knee, pause, lower slowly

exercises.name: Assisted Partial Squat
exercises.summary: A shallow squat with the straps taking some of your weight.
cues: Face the anchor, straps at chest height, arms straight
Sit back to about a quarter squat (60°)
Let the straps take as much weight as you need; drive up through the heels
mistakes: Pulling yourself up with the arms. Arms help; legs do the work

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
exercises.summary: Retrains the knee's sense of position and steadiness.
cues: Stand on one leg near a wall, knee soft, not locked
Keep the hips level and your eyes on a fixed point
Touch the wall only if you need to

exercises.name: Assisted Squat to 90°
exercises.summary: A squat to 90° with the straps helping.
cues: Straps at chest height, lean back slightly
Sit back until the thighs are close to level (90°)
Use less help from the straps each week

exercises.name: Squat to 90°
exercises.summary: An unassisted squat with a chair marking the depth.
cues: Feet shoulder-width, a chair behind you to mark the depth
Sit back until you lightly touch the chair (about 90°)
Stand by pushing through the whole foot

exercises.name: Spanish Squat
exercises.summary: A squat hold with a band behind the knees. Works the thighs hard with little strain on the knee joint.
cues: Loop a heavy band around a sturdy anchor and behind both knees
Step back until the band is tight, feet hip-width
Sit back with the shins upright; hold at a pain-free depth (90° at most)
mistakes: Letting the knees travel forward past the toes

exercises.name: Assisted Split Squat
exercises.summary: The start of single-leg strength, with the straps steadying you.
cues: Hold the straps, one foot forward, back heel up
Lower the back knee straight down a short way
Front knee over the middle toes; push up through the front heel

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.summary: Single-leg strength for stairs and climbing.
cues: Whole foot on a 15–20 cm step
Lean slightly forward; drive through the heel to stand tall
Step back down slowly
mistakes: Pushing off with the bottom leg

exercises.name: Suspension Hamstring Curl
exercises.summary: Strengthens the hamstrings, which help steady the knee.
cues: Lie on your back, heels in the foot cradles, anchor low
Lift the hips into a bridge
Pull the heels toward you by bending the knees, then straighten slowly

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bridge
exercises.summary: Harder glute work, one side at a time.
cues: On your back, one foot planted, the other leg straight in the air
Push through the planted heel to lift the hips, keeping them level
Lower slowly

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.summary: Hip strength for keeping the knee in line. Each rep is one step.
cues: Band above the knees or around the ankles, quarter-squat stance
Step sideways, keeping the band tight and toes facing forward
Don't let the feet come together

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.summary: Calf strength for hopping and landing later.
cues: Stand on one foot, fingertips on a wall
Rise as high as you can, knee straight
Lower over 3 s

exercises.name: Brisk Walk
exercises.summary: Easy fitness work that keeps the knee moving.
cues: A comfortable but purposeful pace
Flat ground first; hills later
Stop if you start limping or pain goes above 3/10

exercises.name: Eyes-Closed Balance
exercises.summary: Balance without help from your eyes.
cues: Stand on one leg next to a wall or in a corner
Find your balance, then close your eyes
Open your eyes or touch the wall to recover, then restart

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.summary: Heavy single-leg strength work.
cues: Back foot on a step or bench behind you
Lower straight down until the front thigh is close to level
Hold the Monkii straps for balance at first, then go without

exercises.name: Forward Step-Down
exercises.summary: Trains slow, controlled lowering. This is also a key test movement.
cues: Stand on a 15–20 cm step, the other leg hanging forward
Lower the free heel toward the floor over 3 s
Tap lightly, then stand back up; knee stays over the middle toes

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat to Box
exercises.summary: A full single-leg squat, with a box or chair marking the depth.
cues: A box or chair behind you, standing on one leg
Sit back slowly to touch the box. Don't drop onto it
Stand up on one leg; hold the Monkii straps for help at first
mistakes: Rocking back and forth to get up

exercises.name: Single-Leg Suspension Curl
exercises.summary: The hamstring curl on one leg at a time.
cues: Set up as for the hamstring curl: one heel in a cradle, other leg raised
Hold the bridge and curl the heel in
Straighten slowly over 3 s

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.summary: Hamstring and glute strength plus balance.
cues: Stand on one leg, knee soft
Hinge at the hip, reaching the hands down as the free leg goes back
Keep the hips square to the floor; squeeze the glute to come back up
mistakes: Hip turning open toward the ceiling

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.summary: Trunk and hip strength for steadier legs.
cues: On your side, elbow under the shoulder
Lift the hips so the body is in a straight line
Start from the knees if you need to

exercises.name: Deep Squat
exercises.summary: Brings back full knee bend gradually, only while it stays pain-free.
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out
Go below 90° only as far as it stays pain-free
Hold the Monkii straps for support at first
mistakes: Pushing deeper through pain or a pinch

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.summary: First impact work: learning to land softly.
cues: Quarter squat, swing the arms
Small jumps at first
Land softly: toes then heels, knees over toes, sink into a squat

exercises.name: Hop and Stick
exercises.summary: Single-leg landing control.
cues: Start with two-leg hops, then progress to one leg
Hop forward a short distance
Hold the landing still for 2 s, knee bent and over the toes

exercises.name: Lateral Hop
exercises.summary: Side-to-side landing control (skater hops).
cues: Jump sideways from one leg to the other
Land softly on the outside leg and hold 1 s
Add distance only when landings are quiet and steady

exercises.name: Deceleration Drill
exercises.summary: Stopping safely from a jog.
cues: Jog 5–10 m
Slow down over 2–3 steps and finish balanced on one leg
Hips back, chest up, knee over the toes

exercises.name: Pivot Drill
exercises.summary: Brings back controlled twisting, the last movement the meniscus gets back.
cues: Stand on one leg, knee slightly bent
Turn 45–90° by pivoting on the ball of the foot
Start slow and small; add speed and angle over the weeks
mistakes: Twisting on a straight, locked knee
Rushing. Any catching or locking means stop
